D010-D006_h001.question:
I’ve been like a storm no one can predict. For the past couple of months, I couldn’t sit still—I was up at 4 a.m. rewriting the entire menu, calling suppliers, launching a catering side business with no plan. I felt electric, like I could run the restaurant, two more, and still have energy to spare. I talked so fast my staff said I was hard to follow. I even flirted aggressively with customers, which isn’t like me… my husband noticed. I spent thousands on glassware and a food truck deposit—just a feeling I *had* to act.  

But then… it crashed. For months now, I can’t get out of bed. I don’t enjoy my daughter’s laughter, I don’t enjoy food—nothing. I stare at my closet for 20 minutes, paralyzed by what to wear. I think… I think my husband is hiding something. I’ve seen him—no, not him, but *shadows* of him—coming out of another room, dressed differently. Other times, I swear I see someone standing at the end of the bar, watching me, but when I look, it’s empty.  

The mood swings—up, down, furious, then numb—have wrecked everything. I don’t know if the voices in my head started during the highs or if they stay after. I can’t tell what’s real anymore, and I don’t know when it began.
D010-D006_h001.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Adjustment Disorder
D010-D006_h001.answer: A & C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D010-D006_h002.question:
I’ve been off for about seven months now—maybe a bit more. It started with this surge of energy last winter. I was up all night, rewriting weather models just for fun, pacing the house, calling colleagues at 3 a.m. to pitch wild ideas. I snapped at my wife over little things—like if she left a mug on the counter. I felt unstoppable. Talked nonstop at work, even interrupted live broadcasts once. Then I invested all our vacation savings into a weather drone startup—didn’t sleep for days after.  

But that high… it faded. I don’t know when exactly. I just stopped going out, stopped calling friends. Even the forecast felt pointless. I started tasting metal all the time—like sucking on a battery—though the doctors can’t find anything wrong. At one point, I became convinced my blood had thickened, that my heart was clogged with sludge. My thoughts feel muddy now, like I’m talking through fog.  

The anger, the energy, the ideas—they’re gone. But so am I, really. I don’t know if the strange tastes and thoughts happened only when I was “up,” or if they’ve stuck around. I can’t tell you how long they lasted without the mania. It’s all blurred.
D010-D006_h002.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Adjustment Disorder
D010-D006_h002.answer: A & C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D010-D006_h003.question:
I’ve just not been myself for a while now—this year especially. There was a stretch, maybe a couple of months back, when I couldn’t sit still. I was pacing the house at all hours, my mind racing, and my wife said I was talking so fast she couldn’t get a word in. Little things set me off—snapping at her over trivial stuff, like the way she folded the laundry. I even drove my old sedan down the highway at night with no destination, windows down, not caring if I got a ticket or wrecked. Looking back, it was reckless.  

But that passed. Then came this heaviness—five months, easy. I couldn’t find joy in anything, not even my garden or my grandkids. I’d just sit and cry, no reason, just tears. Thinking felt thick, like wading through mud.  

And… I’ve been feeling things. Bugs crawling under my skin, but the doctors find nothing. I’m convinced something’s wrong inside—maybe my liver’s rotting or my blood is poisoned, though no test shows it.  

The hard part? I’m not sure when the anger and that buzzing energy started, or if the odd thoughts came before or after. It all blurs together.
D010-D006_h003.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Adjustment Disorder
D010-D006_h003.answer: A & C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D010-D006_h004.question:
I’ve been struggling for a while now—things really started going downhill about seven months ago. At first, I was on fire—working late every night, fixing things around the house at 3 a.m., starting three different side projects. My mind raced so fast I could barely keep up, talking a mile a minute, not sleeping much. I felt brilliant, like I could solve any problem. But then I’d snap—suddenly furious over small things, yelling at my wife for no reason. I was drawn to her physically in a way that felt obsessive, not normal. I drove recklessly, even took some pills a friend offered, just to see what happened.

Then, around two months in, it shifted. I became convinced she was seeing someone else—nothing adds up, but I *know* it’s true. Sometimes, I taste metal, like blood, but there’s nothing there. The energy crashed hard. For the last five months, I’ve just felt… hollow. Can’t focus at work—my boss noticed. Friends stopped calling. I barely talk to anyone. I don’t know if the thoughts are real, or when the highs and lows started blending—I can’t tell what’s me and what’s the illness.
D010-D006_h004.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Adjustment Disorder
D010-D006_h004.answer: A & C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D010-D006_h005.question:
I’ve been off for about the past two months—I don’t know how else to put it. It started with this rush of energy, like I didn’t need sleep, and everything felt *possible*. I was writing all night, ideas spilling out, sentences piling up. I couldn’t stop talking, even when friends told me I was rambling. My body wouldn’t sit still—typing, pacing, rearranging things just to move. 

There was this man at a café—barely knew him—and I ended up at his place. I’ve never been like that before. I wasn’t even attracted to him, really. Just… pulled, like the world was wired straight into me. I flirted with everyone, felt invincible.  

Then the taste came—bitter, metallic, like blood—out of nowhere. No food, nothing. And sometimes I’d hear people on the street drop little phrases, like *they* were meant for me, coded messages in ordinary talk. “Mind your step,” the barista said, and I was sure it meant: *you’re being watched*.  

Now, it’s just… gone. For months, actually. The last five, maybe? I can’t tell. I don’t write. Don’t care. I forget where I leave my keys, my phone—my head’s foggy. I feel hollow, like I’m just going through motions.  
The weird tastes and thoughts? They still flicker—some days more than others—but I can’t say when they start or stop. I don’t know if they’re tied to the highs or just… there.
D010-D006_h005.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Adjustment Disorder
D010-D006_h005.answer: A & C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D010-D006_h006.question:
I’ve been like a runaway train for the past couple of months—maybe longer, I’ve lost track. At first, it felt amazing. I didn’t need sleep—three, four hours max, and I was up, redesigning entire wedding timelines in my head, booking venues overseas like it was nothing. My husband says I was talking a mile a minute, couldn’t let silence happen. If he tried to speak, I’d cut him off, not even realizing. I snapped at brides over tiny details—a shade of blush pink being “off” became a five-alarm fire.

I drove like a maniac to meet vendors, didn’t care about speed limits. Even took cash from the business account to book a villa in Tuscany for a client who hadn’t even signed a contract. I *knew* it made sense—like I was tapped into some higher frequency, like I could see how every moment had to be perfect because I was meant to orchestrate beauty on a global scale. Sometimes, I’d feel fingers tracing my arms at night, even when I was alone. No one’s there—but the sensation? Real as anything. Now that the frenzy’s slowing, I wonder—was any of it real? Or was it just me losing control?
D010-D006_h006.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
D010-D006_h006.answer: D & C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D010-D006_h007.question:
I’ve been like a live wire for the past couple of months—can’t sit still, don’t know if I’m excited or furious at any given moment. One minute I’m on top of the world, telling my manager I’m going to revolutionize the store’s sales in a week, and the next, I’m snapping at customers over nothing. I talk so fast people keep asking me to repeat myself, but even when they do, I just jump into the next thing before finishing. It feels like my brain’s running a marathon I didn’t sign up for.

I’ve driven over 100 miles with no plan, just me and the highway, and once I took a bunch of cash from the register to “invest” in some crypto scheme—I didn’t even know what I was doing. Doesn’t matter. Feels like everything’s urgent.

Lately, I keep thinking something huge is about to happen—not just random stuff, like… the world is collapsing soon. I can feel it. Even now, I swear I feel bugs crawling under my skin, especially at night. I scratch until it bleeds, but they won’t go away. I don’t know when this started or if it’s real. Some days I’m still racing with energy, other days I’m just... numb. But the thoughts and the sensations—they don’t really leave.
D010-D006_h007.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
D010-D006_h007.answer: D & C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D010-D006_h008.question:
I’ve been feeling… on edge for about two months now. It started with not needing much sleep—I could run on three or four hours and still feel wired. I snapped at my staff over tiny things, like a misfolded scarf or a late clock-in, and I *knew* I was overreacting, but I couldn’t stop. My mind races—talking, always talking, and people tell me I don’t make pauses, that I jump topics. I’ve been pacing the store during shifts, rearranging displays at midnight, even when it’s not needed.  

There was this guy I met at a bar—just a hookup, which isn’t like me. I don’t usually do that. I’ve always been careful, but lately… something feels different. Out of control.  

And then there’s this sensation—like fingers brushing my arms when no one’s there. I’ll be alone in my apartment and feel it, sharp and sudden. I know it’s not real, but it *feels* real. I keep thinking my ex is watching me, maybe telling people things. We broke up years ago, but sometimes I’m sure he’s talking about me behind my back, cheating on me all over again—even though I haven’t seen him in ages.  

I can’t tell if it’s the stress of managing the floor during holiday season… or if something’s really wrong. The energy, the thoughts—they don’t feel like *mine*. But I don’t know when it started, or if it’s ever really stopped.
D010-D006_h008.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
D010-D006_h008.answer: D & C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D010-D006_h009.question:
I’ve just turned 53 and lost my husband two years ago—since then, it’s been harder to keep everything together, even though I’ve spent my whole career helping others do the same. Lately, I’ve been feeling… revved up. It started about two months ago—suddenly I wasn’t tired anymore. I’d wake up at 3 a.m., mind racing, and clean the house, reorganize files, call clients even when they didn’t need me. I can’t stop talking, honestly—my friends say I’m like a motor that won’t shut off. I bought seven new outfits last week and three scented candles—none of which I needed. I maxed out a card but keep thinking opportunities are coming.  

And then there’s this smell—like burnt vanilla—no matter where I go. It clings. No one else smells it. I’ve started thinking it’s a sign… that someone’s trying to reach me. This man at the grocery store—he must be sending signals. He doesn’t speak, but I know he feels it too.  

The energy helps at work sometimes, but I’ve snapped at coworkers. I don’t know how long I can keep this pace. The visions and smells—they come and go. So do the highs. I can’t tell when one stops and the other starts.
D010-D006_h009.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
D010-D006_h009.answer: D & C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D010-D006_h010.question:
I’ve been like a live wire for about two months now—can’t sit still, can’t shut my mind off. At work, the other drivers have started to notice. I’ll honk at people for no reason, get into arguments over small things, like someone cutting me off in traffic. I pace during breaks, fidget, feel like I’ve got to keep moving or I’ll explode. I talk constantly—my wife says I don’t let her get a word in, just ramble about ideas, plans, like starting a transportation business, buying a truck, quitting my job tomorrow.  

And I’ve taken chances I never would’ve before—drove 80 down the highway last week, high as I could be on something I got from a guy at the garage. Didn’t care. Felt invincible.  

But it’s not just that. I hear things—voices muttering when no one’s there, like they’re talking about me, judging me. I know it sounds off, but I swear sometimes the radio news anchors are sending me coded messages. My wife says it’s stress, but it feels real. I can’t tell when it started—maybe with the rest of it, maybe after. Hard to say. I just know it won’t stop, and I can’t think straight anymore.
D010-D006_h010.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
D010-D006_h010.answer: D & C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D010-D006_h011.question:
I’ve been feeling like I’m running a thousand miles an hour for about a month now. Work used to be manageable, but lately, I can’t sit still—I’m pacing during calls, snapping at people over tiny things, like if someone sends an email with a typo. I don’t know why it bothers me so much, but it feels like everything is *off*. My mind won’t stop—it jumps from deal structures to geopolitical collapse to old arguments with my dad, and I can’t land on anything.  

There are times, especially at night, when I hear voices—not full conversations, but whispers, like someone’s trying to warn me. And I keep getting this feeling… that none of it will matter soon. Like the markets are rigged, the city’s crumbling, and we’re all just moving toward some kind of end. It’s not a thought I believe logically, but it sits in my chest like a weight.  

I’m still showing up, but I know I’m not functioning right. I haven’t slept more than three hours a few nights because my body feels like it doesn’t need to. But whether these voices and thoughts started during the high or have lingered beyond it… I can’t quite tell. It’s all just been one long blur.
D010-D006_h011.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D010-D006_h011.answer: B & D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D010-D006_h012.question:
I’ve been feeling… different for about a month now, maybe a little longer—hard to tell. At first, I was super charged, like I’d had eight coffees and no exhaustion. I’d show up to the job site early, bouncing between tasks—running wires, sketching out circuit ideas, helping coworkers even when it wasn’t my job. Felt like I could do ten things at once and still have energy left. My brain wouldn’t shut up—thoughts jumping everywhere, like radio stations flipping every few seconds. 

But then… I started noticing things. People on the bus laughing, and I just *knew* it was about me—coded jokes, glances, like they were sending signals. Once, I swear I heard my foreman’s voice behind me, saying I wasn’t safe around electricity, but when I turned, no one was there. It's happened a few times, mostly voices commenting when I’m alone.  

The high energy? It's faded, but the thoughts and sounds… they haven’t fully gone. Some days are clear, others, not so much. I don’t know if it was all part of the same thing or… separate. I’m still showing up to work, but I know I’m not right.

A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D010-D006_h013.question:

My mind races like ten TVs are on at once—thoughts crashing into each other, like I’m trying to close a deal while arguing with my husband and planning an open house all in my head. And then there are these… things I see. Out the corner of my eye—someone standing at the edge of listings I’m reviewing, a figure outside a property at dusk. I know it doesn’t make sense, but I *see* them. I also feel sure that… well, there’s this broker I barely know, but I’m convinced he’s been sending me signals—he *has* to be in love with me. Little glances, timing our showings… it can’t be random. My husband thinks I’m losing it, and honestly, some days I do too. I keep going because I have to, but I’m not sure when any of this started—or if it ever really stops.

D010-D006_h015.question:
I’ve been feeling really off for about a month now—maybe a bit longer, it’s hard to track. It’s not just stress—there’s this constant buzz in my body, like I can’t sit still even when I’m exhausted. I feel like she’s reaching out, that she *knows* me on a deeper level. It makes sense to me, even if others wouldn’t.  

I haven’t been sleeping much, but I don’t feel tired. I keep applying to jobs, but I can’t focus long enough to finish applications. I don’t know if it’s all connected or if I’m losing grip—but it’s been this way for weeks, and I can’t seem to reset.

A. Bipolar II Disorder

    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D010-D006_h016.question:
I’ve been off for a while now—about seven months, I guess—just not myself. Most days I can’t get out of bed, even after sleeping 12 hours. I feel heavy, like there’s no point. I’ve stopped going to the card games with the guys from the post, and my wife says I don’t talk to her like I used to. Sometimes I think, “Wouldn’t it be easier if I just didn’t wake up?” I don’t want to hurt myself, but I’m tired.  

Then, about three weeks ago, something shifted. I didn’t need sleep. I was full of ideas—starting projects at home, talking fast, couldn’t stop talking, really. My wife says I wouldn’t let her get a word in. I felt sharp, powerful, like I could see things others couldn’t. Like people on the street were sending me messages—certain smells from passing cars meant something, warnings maybe. I kept smelling something burning, like wire insulation, but no one else did.  

Now the energy’s fading, but I’m confused. Were those messages real then? Did I lose it? I used to handle my post just fine—steady, alert—but now I’m scared I’ll mess up. The thoughts come and go. I don’t know when it started or what’s what anymore.
D010-D006_h016.options:

D010-D006_h017.question:

D010-D006_h018.question:

D010-D006_h019.question:

    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D010-D006_h020.question:

I stopped going to book club, didn’t feel like cooking, barely touched my garden. Things I’ve always loved—just didn’t matter anymore. And I kept thinking, *What’s the point? My husband says I’ve been pacing the house at night, snapping over little things—burning dinner, dropping dishes, just losing my temper. I can’t seem to slow down. Words spill out before I can catch them; he says he can’t get a word in.

And… I know it sounds strange, but I’ve been hearing whispers when no one’s there, like someone’s murmuring behind a door. I also feel like something’s terribly wrong inside me—my heart’s rotting, or my blood’s poisoned. The doctor finds nothing, but I *know* it’s happening. When I’m low, the voices fade, but the dread stays. When I’m wired like this, everything feels sharper—even the sickness inside.
D010-D006_h020.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D010-D006_h020.answer: C & D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D010-D006_h021.question:
I’ve been off since early summer—about two weeks of not sleeping more than two hours a night, but I didn’t feel tired. I was rearranging classroom supplies at midnight, furious if a parent was a minute late picking up their kid. Everything felt irritating—small noises, slow conversations, even the way someone folded a paper towel. I couldn’t focus during circle time; my thoughts raced, jumping from lesson plans to redesigning the whole school. I remember seeing shadows move in the corners of the room, like figures squatting behind the bookshelf, but when I turned, nothing was there.  

Then, things just… dropped. By fall, I couldn’t get out of bed. Moving felt like pushing through wet cement. I stopped caring that I hadn’t updated my portfolio—no energy, no point. I thought about ending it all, figured I could take pills when the apartment was empty, Saturday morning maybe. I even checked the lock on the medicine cabinet.  

The jealous thoughts about my ex started around then—I kept thinking he was meeting someone new, hiding her in *our* coffee shop. I never saw her face, but I *knew* she was there. I can’t say exactly how long the rage or the sadness lasted—time blurred. Some days I felt wired again, but not quite like before.
D010-D006_h021.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D010-D006_h021.answer: B & A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D010-D006_h022.question:
I’ve been a dancer since I was three, and this past year has been… unrecognizable. For about two weeks last spring, I couldn’t sleep—like, not at all—and I didn’t even want to. I’d wake up buzzing, like my blood was full of electricity. I rehearsed all day, then went to clubs, dancing until dawn. My mind jumped from one idea to ten others—choreography, world tours, messages from the universe hidden in music notes—but I couldn’t stick with anything more than a few minutes. I snapped at my director over tiny corrections. One time, I swear I felt hands adjusting my arms during rehearsal, like invisible hands guiding me—no one was there.

Then it crashed. For months, just getting out of bed felt impossible. I stopped coming to the studio. My limbs moved through mud. I filled a bag with pills one night. I didn’t take them—couldn’t even muster the energy, honestly—but I knew I wanted to.  

Now? I don’t know what’s real. I still feel those touches sometimes. And part of me still believes—*knows*—I’m meant to transcend the stage, that I’m not just a dancer. But I can’t tell if that’s truth, or the illness, or both.
D010-D006_h022.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D010-D006_h022.answer: B & A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D010-D006_h023.question:
I’ve been going through something really intense lately—about two weeks ago, I suddenly felt *amazing*. Not just happy, but like I could fix anything, anytime. I was jumping from job to job, barely sleeping, my hands wouldn’t stop moving, always tinkering with tools or rerouting elevator circuits even when they didn’t need it. My mind raced—I’d start a task, then get distracted by a noise, a thought, a flash of light. I couldn’t focus, but I didn’t care—everything felt urgent and exciting.  

During that time, I started hearing my supervisor’s voice when he wasn’t around. He’d whisper how proud he was of me, how I was changing the building’s energy. I knew it wasn’t real, but... it felt true. I became convinced his daughter was secretly in love with me—we’ve only said “hi” twice, but I’d catch her staring, and the voices confirmed it.  

But then it crashed. Two months now, I can’t get out of bed. Moving feels like dragging concrete. I look at my work bag and just… freeze. I think, “What’s the point?” Sometimes I hope I won’t wake up. The voices still come, quiet now, saying I’m a failure.  

I don’t know when it started or if it ever really stops. The highs fade fast, but the voices? They linger. Or maybe they don’t. I can’t tell anymore.
D010-D006_h023.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D010-D006_h023.answer: B & A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D010-D006_h024.question:
I’ve been feeling completely off for the past couple of months—maybe longer. Some days, I’m wired, like my brain’s running ten miles a minute. I’ll start three investigations at once, dig into surveillance footage, track people down, but never finish any of it. I can’t sit still—pacing, fidgeting, like there’s electricity under my skin. My moods swing hard, too. One minute I’m on top of the world, the next I’m snapping at clients for no reason.  

But then… it crashes. Lately, I haven’t cared about anything—not the cases, not the gym, not even my dog. I used to love tailing suspects, cracking cases—now it all feels pointless. I pace at night, can’t sleep. Sometimes I hear voices—low, talking just behind me, saying I’m being watched. And maybe I am. I’ve been certain my phone’s tapped, that someone’s following me, watching from unmarked cars. Can’t prove it, but I *know*.  

A few times, standing on my apartment balcony, I’ve had this sudden urge to step off—no plan, no note, just… a pull. Scared me so bad I locked the door. I don’t know if I’m manic, psychotic, or just unraveling. The truth? I can’t tell when the mania ends and the fear begins.
D010-D006_h024.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D010-D006_h024.answer: B & A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D010-D006_h025.question:
I’ve been through some highs and lows lately—more than I can remember having in years. About two weeks straight a few months back, I felt incredible—like I’d tapped into something brilliant. I was writing three books at once, pacing around the house at all hours, barely sleeping. My wife says I couldn’t finish a sentence without jumping to a new idea. I started rewriting old manuscripts, designing covers, even pitching TV adaptations—none of which I ever followed through on.  

Then it all crashed. For two months, I couldn’t get out of my chair. Moving felt like wading through mud. I stopped writing altogether, not because I didn’t care about my work, but because success suddenly seemed meaningless. I kept thinking, “Does any of this matter?” I wouldn’t mind if I didn’t wake up one morning.  

The strange part? I started tasting pennies—even when I wasn’t eating anything. And sometimes, I’d hear neighbors laughing and just *know* they were mocking sentences from my unpublished novels. I can’t say for sure if they were. I haven’t told my wife those parts.  

The timing… I can’t quite place it—whether the voices came only during the high, or lingered after. It’s all blurred.
D010-D006_h025.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D010-D006_h025.answer: B & A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
